archive.scope: local synthetic SeaweedFS evidence; not AWS or production SLO

interpretation: All 1673 observed resource rejections first hit the original tenant request-intake counter at used=40, limit=40, requested=1; this is not proof of the sole throughput bottleneck.
Keep default group commit disabled and current quotas/lifetimes; no retry, original-ETag refresh, persistence barrier or ACK change.
No rejection at 12 arrivals/s does not establish sustainable service capacity: unfinished client requests accumulated and every medium phase drained beyond the fixed 16-second arrival window.

The second long contended pair improved ACK/drain throughput while ACK fell 173 to 165 and within-window ACK fell 133 to 125; starting rows/pages/retained identities were also unequal (242/20/243 versus 256/21/257).
Total S3 requests in the first long contended pair increased 3263 to 3418; second-pair request/response body bytes per ACK increased approximately 1.28%/1.46%, despite fewer requests per ACK.
Control probe success is not a latency improvement guarantee; first long contended pair maximum increased from 54.162159ms to 127.269458ms, with only four probes per stage.
Public arrival/HTTP timing and concurrent HEAD groups do not expose internal locked gate timestamps or establish causal attribution.
Original raw source, HTTP/S3 bytes, random witnesses, failures, exact binary/native archive and unit LLVM report are retained in the hashed external archive; raw records are not committed to Git.
